claim: For every finite set D of distinct integers at least 3 with gcd(D)=1 and sigma(D)=sum_{d in D}1/(d-1)>=1, every integer k>=1, and every finite set F of labelled occurrences (d,j) with d in D and j>=k, list the remaining occurrences by increasing value and then increasing base label as a_1,a_2,... and put S_m=sum_{i=1}^m a_i; then S_m-a_{m+1} tends to positive infinity as m tends to infinity.

quadruple.statement: For each admissible labelled stream, bounded-gap next-power pairs for a pair distinguished by prime support form a finite-rank linear-incidence image with only finitely many points below any fixed gap bound; the exact geometric-sum identity pulls this finiteness back to the original all-future surplus limit.
quadruple.stage: Fixed-coefficient linear incidences in finite-rank subgroups of the multiplicative torus over the algebraic closure of Q, with a labelled integer-stream pull-back.

shape.objects: Finite sets D, positive integer cutoffs k, finite sets of deleted labelled pairs, and an infinite locally finite ordered power stream. Finset, Nat powers, finite sums and order filters have Lean/Mathlib definitions. Inputs are streams and lower-bound parameters, not a class of representation solutions. No seed-amplification construction of the all-future threshold is known, and no continuous deformation or probabilistic ensemble is part of this claim.
shape.quantifiers: For every admissible finite D, every positive integer k, every finite deletion F, and every real B, there exists m_0>=1 such that S_m-a_{m+1}>B for every m>=m_0; distinct labelled occurrences remain separately available even when their values coincide.
shape.target_quantity: A qualitative divergence decision, equivalently eventual passage above every fixed real lower bound. An unspecified threshold for each input and bound suffices; no numerical optimum or effective threshold is required.
shape.ambient_structure: Integer additive order and multiplicative prime-factor structure coexist. The prospective map encodes bounded differences of powers as fixed-coefficient linear incidences in a finite-rank multiplicative subgroup. No recursive operation constructing certified all-future thresholds, probabilistic dependence parameter, bias statistic, or continuous transport path is recorded.
shape.symmetries: Relabelling bases does not alter the ordered numerical sequence apart from tie order. All tied values remain distinct occurrences. No family of structured pieces closed under translation, dilation and intersection is being used.
shape.configuration: The required relation is S_m-a_{m+1}>B at every sufficiently late prefix. Its exact residual is an additive relation among next unused powers. Discarding a finite prefix changes the eventual sums by a fixed constant and does not itself obstruct a divergence property. No finite extension operation is known to preserve a certified all-future lower bound from one finite seed.
shape.extremal_candidate: No extremal counterexample or opposite-side construction is recorded. Equal powers of different bases are a real obstruction to a naive all-pair gap assertion and must not be treated as distinct numerical values.
shape.finite_certificates: Each specified prefix has an exactly evaluable sum and next term, but neither truth nor failure of this infinite divergence assertion has a known finite certificate. Computable finite prefix examples are not a certificate for every later index and are not admitted for execution.
shape.monotonicity: For fixed input, eventual passage above B becomes weaker as B decreases. The desired lower bounds B are unbounded and no distinguished smallest open B is supplied.
shape.uniformity_parameter: Every admissible finite D, positive k and finite F, including reciprocal mass exactly one; thresholds may depend on these inputs and B.

Every quantifier and tie case is explicit. No computation or numerical optimisation interface is used.
